title: Population & migration
examples: What makes one country's population grow faster than another's?
How does the age structure of a population affect its economy?
Can you give an example of a push factor and a pull factor?

explain.say: Today we will look at how populations change over time. We will also explore why people move from one place to another.

items: Birth Rate > Death Rate: Population Growth

explain.say: Population growth happens when the birth rate is higher than the death rate. For example, a high birth rate means many babies are born in a short time.
Population structure shows the age makeup of a country. For instance, a large number of young people suggests future workforce growth.
Migration involves people moving across borders. A push factor is something that forces people to leave their home area.

draw.text: Migration: Push Factors Force People Out

explain.say: A pull factor is something that attracts people to a new location. For example, job opportunities in a city can pull people there.
In everyday life, think about people moving to a city for work. The job is the pull factor, while rural poverty might be the push factor.

faq.q: What is the difference between a push factor and a pull factor?
faq.a: A push factor is a negative condition that makes people want to leave a place. A pull factor is a positive condition that attracts people to a new place.
asks: What makes people leave their homes?
What attracts people to new countries?

faq.q: How does a country's age structure affect its economy?
faq.a: A structure with many working-age people supports a strong economy. Too many elderly people can strain resources.
asks: Why is the age pyramid important for planning?
What does a young population mean for jobs?

faq.q: Is high population growth always good for a country?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Rapid growth can strain resources like clean water and food supplies.
asks: Can too many people cause problems?
What are the downsides of a growing population?

faq.q: What is 'natural increase' in population terms?
faq.a: Natural increase is simply the number of live births minus the number of deaths in a specific area.
asks: How do you calculate population growth?
What is the difference between births and deaths?

faq.q: Do all migrants move for the same reasons?
faq.a: No, people migrate for complex reasons, often involving a combination of push and pull factors working together.
asks: Can people move for reasons other than jobs?

facts: A high birth rate compared to a low death rate causes population growth.
The age structure shows the proportion of young, working, and old people.
Push factors are negative reasons forcing people to leave a place.
Pull factors are positive attractions drawing people to a new place.

quiz.say: A country has many young people and few elderly people. This suggests:
quiz.why: This structure means many people will enter the working age group soon.

wrong.1: This is wrong because a large young population usually means a growing workforce.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the structure shows few people are in the older age brackets.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the structure implies that births are currently high.

quiz.say: If a region suffers from severe drought and famine, this is an example of a:
quiz.why: Famine and drought are negative conditions that force people to leave their homes.

wrong.0: This is wrong because it describes a rate, not a reason for movement.
wrong.1: This is wrong because age structure describes age groups within a population.
wrong.3: This is wrong because pull factors are positive attractions, not negative forces.

quiz.say: A new city offers excellent universities and high wages. This is best described as:
quiz.why: Excellent universities and high wages are positive attractions drawing people in.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the description suggests a reason for people to move toward the area.
wrong.2: This is wrong because push factors are negative reasons to leave, not positive reasons to arrive.
wrong.3: This is wrong because natural increase is about births minus deaths, not attraction.
